subject.title: feat(auto-reply): add "commentary" verbose level for narration-only progress

question: Should `commentary` remain a session-scoped `/verbose` preset, or also become a valid global/per-agent `verboseDefault` despite older releases rejecting that config on downgrade?
rationale: The runtime lane split is technically sound, but no implementation can make an already-released strict schema accept a future enum value; accepting the config surface is therefore a product and rollback-policy decision.

options.title: Keep it session-scoped
options.body: Remove `commentary` from global/per-agent config schemas and docs while retaining the persisted session command and UI selection, which older runtimes tolerate as an unknown session value.

options.title: Accept the config break
options.body: Keep the new default value only with explicit maintainer approval, clear minimum-version and rollback documentation, and fresh-install plus downgrade proof showing the intended failure and recovery path.

options.title: Decline the core preset
options.body: Close this direction and rely on channel-specific controls such as the merged Slack commentary setting where operators need independent progress lanes.

recommendation.title: Keep it session-scoped
recommendation.body: Remove `commentary` from global/per-agent config schemas and docs while retaining the persisted session command and UI selection, which older runtimes tolerate as an unknown session value.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work introduced the shared commentary-progress behavior that defines the core product boundary being extended here.
